audit.title: Fetch and decode Data Streams reports using the Rust SDK

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Sections open procedurally rather than with a liftable claim; the page has no TL;DR. The Explanation subsections are well-scoped and self-contained. Weak: opening paragraph is a task promise, not a canonical statement.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong — 13 headings, 1 H1, 0 level skips, median 71 words/section, max 531, none over 600 (measured). Clean H2/H3/H4 hierarchy and a well-formed attribute table. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Good code-level specifics (SDK `1.0.3`, `tokio 1.4`, real timestamps, 18-decimal prices, testnet URLs). Weak: measured "version strings [none]" in prose and vague quantifiers "several, most, robust" present.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Strong — 28 links, 7 to primary sources (rust-lang.org, github.com), with deep links to exact SDK source lines (`config.rs#L131`). No action needed.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Attribute table gives crisp per-field definitions. Weak: no one-sentence liftable definition of the Rust SDK itself or of `decode_full_report`'s role near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak — measured 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags. Head could not be verified; CLI should pass raw `<head>` to confirm. This is the largest single scored gap.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Excellent — 9 fenced blocks, 0 untagged, full `main.rs` with imports, `Cargo.toml`, run command, and expected output. Minor: the second Rust config excerpt omits imports (measured 1 of 2 import-needing blocks shows none), acceptable as an excerpt.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers setup → fetch → decode → adapt → explain. Weak: no troubleshooting/FAQ section and no headings phrased as the errors/questions devs type (e.g. `API_KEY must be set`, "invalid feed ID", "which report version do I use").

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Fluent and consistent. Minor: "feed ID" vs "Stream ID" used for the same value may confuse entity resolution.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured Rust tutorial with a complete, copy-pasteable end-to-end example, pinned dependency versions, expected terminal output, and github source links into the SDK — genuinely agent-runnable. Its biggest GEO weakness is discoverability: no JSON-LD/`TechArticle` schema or canonical URL in the served HTML, and no symptom- or question-phrased headings that match how developers actually query (error strings, "how do I decode a v8 report"). The headline verdict: strong content that will convert well *if retrieved*, but under-instrumented for retrieval and missing troubleshooting coverage.

recommendations.title: Add a troubleshooting section with symptom-phrased H3s
recommendations.where: new section after "Adapting code for different report schema versions"
recommendations.issue: no error-string or "how do I…" headings; devs/agents query by symptom.
recommendations.change: add H3s like `### "API_KEY must be set" panic`, `### Decoding fails / wrong fields returned (report version mismatch)`, `### Invalid feed ID format`, each with a one-line cause and fix.
recommendations.why: headings matching literal error text win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses, even when the answer is already in body text.

recommendations.title: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD + canonical URL + last-updated
recommendations.issue: measured 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `programmingLanguage: Rust`, `dateModified`, and a canonical `<link>`; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-ability and E-E-A-T trust for engines and agents.

recommendations.title: Lead the page with a liftable canonical statement
recommendations.issue: opens as a task promise ("you'll learn how to…"), not a self-contained fact.
recommendations.change: prepend one sentence: "The Chainlink Data Streams Rust SDK (`chainlink-data-streams-sdk` v1.0.3) fetches and decodes signed reports from the Data Streams Aggregation Network over a REST/WebSocket API."
recommendations.why: a crisp, verbatim-liftable definition in the first chunk defends against parametric priors and is quoted more often.

recommendations.title: Name the version-mismatch failure as an explicit Don't
recommendations.where: "Adapting code for different report schema versions"
recommendations.issue: current guidance is soft ("make sure to adjust").
recommendations.change: add a bold Don't line: "Don't decode a v8 stream with `ReportDataV3::decode` — it silently mis-parses fields. Match the `ReportDataVn` decoder to the stream's schema version."
recommendations.why: naming the tempting-wrong pattern explicitly stops engines from synthesizing the generic (wrong) approach.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with specifics
recommendations.issue: "The SDK provides several methods", "Rust's robust error handling".
recommendations.change: "provides two REST methods (`get_latest_report`, `get_report`)"; drop "robust" or replace with the concrete mechanism.
recommendations.why: quantified, specific prose outperforms qualitative filler in generative retrieval.

recommendations.title: Normalize the feed ID / Stream ID terminology
recommendations.issue: same `0x0003…` value is called both "feed ID" and "Stream ID".
recommendations.change: state once that the terms are interchangeable, or standardize on one.
recommendations.why: consistent entity naming improves entity resolution and reduces ambiguous synthesis.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers "several", "most", "robust" (measured) — minor, addressed in P3.
Unassigned identifiers `API_KEY`/`API_SECRET` in code (measured) — acceptable here; they are documented env vars set via `export`, not a real gap.
No stale-content risk visible, but absence of a dateModified means freshness can't be signaled — covered in P1.
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical, and og/twitter tags are site-template concerns; the page references `/llms.txt`, which is good — confirm this tutorial is indexed there.
Head metadata could not be verified from the captured content; re-run with raw `<head>` passed through for a definitive metadata read.
Deep internal links into this page from the Rust SDK reference and crypto-streams pages would strengthen its canonical-hub standing (earned/internal-link factor).
